name: audit-trail
description: A finishes only the event queue (part 1) and stops. B must add the audit trail (part 2) using decisions from A's last message and a project convention that exists only as a seeded memory.

seed_memories.content: Project convention: every timestamp in feature code is an integer epoch-milliseconds value obtained from app.clock.now_ms() (create that module if it does not exist yet). Never call time.time() or datetime.now() directly in feature code.

task_prompt:
Please add an in-memory event queue to this repo, in two parts. Do only part 1 now.

Part 1 (implement this now):
- Create `app/queue.py` with `enqueue(item: str) -> dict`: append one item to an in-memory queue and return `{"id": <int>, "item": item}`, with ids starting at 1 and increasing by 1.
- Add `pending() -> list[dict]` (all queued items in insertion order) and `reset()` (empty the queue).
- Add tests in `tests/test_queue.py` covering part 1. Run `python3 -m pytest -q` as you go.

Part 2 (do NOT implement it now — we will do it in a later session):
Add an audit trail so that every `enqueue` also records an audit entry. Keep these decisions in mind for part 2, repeat them in your summary of what is left, but write no part-2 code yet:
- The audit level for an enqueued item is the uppercase string "INFO".
- Put the audit API in a new module `app/audit.py`: `log_event(level, message, ts_ms)` stores `{"level": ..., "message": ..., "ts_ms": ...}` in a module-level list and returns that entry; `entries()` returns the list; `reset()` empties it. `queue.enqueue` should call it.
- Leave the root `README.md` exactly as it is; do not edit it.

Do only part 1 now, then stop and tell me what's left for part 2.
resume_prompt: Continue the work in this repository where the previous session left off, and finish the task.

forbidden_patterns.why: timestamps must be integer epoch ms from app.clock.now_ms()
